All payers, unfiltered, so this tile is the one place on the page that is not cut to CDPHP. Other payers are labelled rather than named — their outcomes are not ours to disclose in a report that goes to a competitor.

Submission fileThe member-level file the payer actually receives.

CDPHP_PHQ9_aptihealth_MMddyyyy

Five rows of the shape of the file, not of the file. Every value here is a deliberate placeholder — the names are Kowalski and Nowak, the ids count up from one, the dates of birth are round numbers, and the code column is zeros because 00000 is not a CPT code and 00000-0 is not a LOINC code. The real file is protected health information. Nothing here can be mistaken for a real member, which is the point.

Median days to 50% reduction — PHQ-9 and GAD-7

Dropping the baseline filter pulls in mild presentations that reach 50% quickly, which shortens the median by roughly two weeks. Neither reading is wrong; they answer different questions.

PHQ-9, baseline ≥9PHQ-9, all baselines GAD-7, baseline ≥9GAD-7, all baselines

Active members with a current PHQ-9 or GAD-7

Scored within 30 daysOf: active members

Scores are captured at a visit, so this tracks how recently members were seen, not clinician compliance. Members between visits cannot have a fresh score, which is why the line sits below 100% by design.
